title: Task paradigm
_readme: A paradigm is a SHAPE: which knobs a kind of experiment fixes, and what the
wizard should ask about everything else. It is deliberately weaker than a
spec and must stay that way.
WHAT IT MAY NOT DECLARE, and why `additionalProperties: false` matters more
here than usual: no `nodes` (D1 -- the template emits them), no timing VALUE
(the template owns the defaults, the operator owns the values), no strobe
code (the vocabulary owns those), and no channel name (the pinout does).
Every one of those would make this file a second, weaker spec format, and
the whole argument for generating a skeleton is that the generator defines

affords.description: One or two sentences: what this paradigm lets you measure. Shown on the gallery card and used as the generated spec's meta.description.

order.description: Gallery order. Explicit rather than alphabetical, so the canonical paradigm leads and self_check() has a defined probe.

topology.description: The knobs this paradigm FIXES. A knob omitted here takes the template's default and may be moved afterwards in the Designer.

response_ports.description: A COUNT, never names. The generator binds this many `kind: response` channels from the active pinout, in registry order, so a paradigm never mentions a pin.

contingency.description: The contingency SKELETON: counts and shape, never values.

stimuli.description: How many stimuli to declare. Emitter lines and onset codes come from the registries.

rewarded.description: Whether a correct trial delivers. The one layer-2 field that changes the GRAPH: null omits the delivery PULSE and the consumption WAIT_EXIT.

trial_types.description: The stimulus-to-answer mapping. An enum rather than a structure, so this file cannot grow an index-into-index format.

weight_one_only.description: Shaping: build every arm but offer one. Turning a weight up later is a policy edit rather than a reshape.

ramped.description: Timing ids this paradigm expects to ramp across a stage schedule. Names ids only -- the VALUES and the trial boundaries are the operator's.

questions.description: What the wizard asks, in order. Every path is a document path the spec schema already knows, so an answer is a set on a validated location and never new structure.

source.description: Where the offered options come from. `value` is free text or a number.

kind.description: For source=channel: which channel kind to offer.
